To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the skin of trout, O. mykiss, exposed to water of pH=5, exhibited a series of structural and cellular changes that included the following: 1) the epidermis became thinner and degenerative cells became common; 2) many apoptotic lymphocytes and leucocytes appeared in the epidermal layers; 3) mucous cells became elongate; 4) the number of iridocytes decreased; and 5) the dermis became thickened,

acid exposure of rainbow trout resulted in changes in epidermal and dermal structure of the skin, and that the plasma cortisol level of the fish increased after 1 day of acid exposure, and returned to control values after 7 days of acid exposure.

acidified water induced a significant elevation of plasma cortisol levels, and a significant thinning of the epidermal layer in the skin, with the formation of degenerative cells, and the appearance of apoptotic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
cellular responses of the skin of fish exposed to acidified waters.
the effects of low pH on the structure of the skin, and the plasma cortisol concentration in trout.
cellular responses in the skin of trout, Oncoryhnchus mykiss.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the skin of acid-exposed trout exhibited signs of stress and damage, but that the skin structure had not been completely destroyed.

the acid-induced changes in the skin of trout are similar to those seen in the skin of salmon exposed to low salinities, but the effects of low pH on the plasma cortisol levels are opposite to those of low salinity.
the epidermis is more sensitive to low pH than the dermis, but both layers are affected, as are the plasma cortisol levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the skin of the rainbow trout responds to exposure to acidified fresh water in a way which may be similar to the responses in mammals, but that the changes occur at a slower pace.
the skin of trout exposed to acidified freshwater is a dynamic structure, which is able to adapt itself to the new conditions.
exposure of fish to acidified water causes a series of changes in the skin, and that the plasma cortisol level is elevated in response to this stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trout are able to mount a rapid response to acid exposure, but this response is insufficient to counteract the effects of acid on the skin structure.
trout skin responds rapidly to acid exposure, with changes in cell morphology and function, but the plasma cortisol level is not a good indicator of skin damage.
exposure to acidified waters may induce stress and cause changes in the skin of rainbow trout.
